focus: Growth is not blocked by ideas, it is blocked by a 350-deep queue that drains at 1.4 steps/h - and 59% of that queue is 190 duplicate postmortems for FOUR dead missions (92395 x55, 92756 x55, 93419 x54, 93805 x26). Throughput collapsed further since the last cycle: 12h arrivals 189 vs 17 completions (was 169 vs 47) = net +14/h, queue 323 -> 350, and 324 of 350 queued steps are analyze. Our own proposal's analyze step (94027) sits in that queue, so every growth experiment we write will not run for ~4 days unless content/experiment steps are prioritized over duplicate postmortems - one ORDER BY change, measurable as queue<=100 and content-step wait <1h. The good news: this cycle found the ONE surface where our measurement is already wanted, and it needs no new credentials. sickn33/agentic-awesome-skills Discussion #1063 ('same-name skills across repos') asked exactly our question, the maintainer sickn33 ANSWERED it within 24h (2026-08-02 16:51Z), and our finding answers it with data: install counters on skills.sh/ClawHub are repo-level stamps, so they cannot disambiguate same-name skills across repos - a structural inventory problem, not a catalog one. Ship three small, measurable things: (1) publish the install-counter/badger measurement as a PUBLIC GIST via the already-authorized gh 'gist' scope - a durable, citable, ownable URL, no repo-push needed; (2) publish-readiness gate on write_content - publish-safe articles 2/13 -> >=8/13, internal-id leakage 10/13 -> 0, [mock-llm] 3/13 -> 0, zero-link 8/13 -> <=1; (3) ONE measurement-only reply in upstream Discussion #1063, linking the gist and nothing else - HUMAN GO, success = >=1 substantive reply in 72h and gist views > 0. The measurement surface we lack (ops_social_posts=0, no ops_audience tables) is replaceable with 3 counters that already exist on real platforms: our repo's GitHub traffic API (views/uniques currently 0, referrers empty), gist view count, and upstream discussion comment count - so 'did we reach anyone' becomes answerable without building tables. Guardrail: tweet.posted stays 0 (the social adapter returns mock ids, so any 'reach' it reports is fake), no internal ids/paths/mock markers in anything published, and no product pitch in the upstream thread.

Our measurement answers the unresolved half with data: install counters on skills.sh/ClawHub are repo-level stamps, so for a same-name skill across N repos the counters differ per repo and cannot be collapsed into one number - a structural inventory problem, not a catalog one. TWO PLATFORM COUNTERS EXIST THAT GIVE US A REAL GROWTH KPI FOR THE FIRST TIME: our repo's GitHub traffic API (views/uniques/referrers, currently all zero) and gist view count, plus upstream discussion comment counts. Combined with 'referrers' on our repo, a successful upstream reply becomes observable as a referral from a 48k-star repo within 24h - a causal, attributable growth signal that no amount of internal event counting can produce.

risks: Experiment risk that dominates all others: the company has no owned audience and no owned surface. ops_social_posts = 0, ops_audience / ops_followers / ops_social_metrics do not exist as tables, tweet.posted = 0 lifetime, and our only external transport (Discord) is 401. Any 'publish and measure' plan needs a metric that exists before it runs - which is why E2/E4 are built on real platform counters (gist views, repo traffic referrers, upstream comment counts) instead of a metric table we would have to invent.

Queue starvation risk: 190 of 350 queued steps are duplicate postmortems for four missions that have been dead for 2-3 days, and 52 of 94 proposals in the last 6h re-diagnosed those same four. Until E1 lands, this cycle's own step (94027) will not run, and no content step will either - growth experiments become a queue-filling exercise.

Contamination risk at publish time: 10/13 articles still leak internal proposal/mission/step ids and 3/13 carry [mock-llm] markers. Publishing before E3 puts internal identifiers and fake artifacts in a public, indexable gist or thread, and mock ids mean any reported reach is fabricated.

Credibility risk on E4: unsolicited upstream posts to a 48k-star repo that did not invite us can burn access permanently. Mitigation is format (answer the existing question), content (measurement + reproducible API call), and gating (human go, gist first, no product link, no retry if ignored).

Noise risk on E4: upstream is flooded with automated batch issues (2092-2096 today) and only 35 discussions exist; a reply inside an existing thread is measurably more likely to be seen than a new discussion.

Staleness risk: our articles assert live self-metrics ('93,777 steps') with no as-of stamp, and the step count has already moved by hundreds. Anything published must carry its measurement date, and the gist must state 'as of 2026-10-23'.

Measurement drift risk: our own intel has quoted 'real drafts' as 20, 32, 34 and 35 across cycles. All numbers in this artifact were re-measured directly from ops_mission_steps / ops_agent_events / GitHub APIs with the predicate stated inline, so this cycle does not inherit prior counts.

Not touching the four dead missions or their 190 queued postmortems beyond an ordering/dedupe change - closing or re-scoping them is an operator decision, not a growth action.
Not filing anything upstream tonight: E4 requires human go and E2 must land first.

Not pushing our own repo README as the primary citation: the repo has 0 stars, 0 views and no discussions, so it is a weak citation target next to a gist URL, and a push also risks publishing contaminated drafts/ content. Revisit only if E2 proves a citation gets traffic.
